proposal: The Mandate recommends reversing the prior administration's non-enforcement of Section 117 of the Higher Education Act, which requires colleges to report foreign gifts and contracts of $250,000 or more. It calls for investigating institutions that fail to comply and referring them to the Department of Justice, and for working with Congress to tie foreign-source reporting compliance to eligibility for federal aid, particularly under Titles IV and VI.

status_summary: The executive parts are under way. Executive Order 14282 (signed 2025-04-23) directs the Education Secretary to enforce Section 117, conduct audits and investigations and seek enforcement through the Attorney General, and makes compliance a condition for federal grants. ED returned enforcement to its Office of General Counsel and opened investigations of Harvard (2025-04-17), UC Berkeley (announced 2025-04-25) and Penn (2025-05-08); CRS counted four investigations as of March 2026, and a press report of 2026-09-17 describes reviews of Duke and the University of North Dakota. ED opened a new reporting portal in January 2026 and signed an agreement with the State Department on 2026-02-20 to administer reporting and civil investigations. The statutory link to aid eligibility is not law: the DETERRENT Act (H.R. 1048) passed the House 241 to 169 on 2025-03-27 with no reported Senate action, and no DOJ referral was found.

timeline.event: The House passed H.R. 1048, the DETERRENT Act, 241 to 169; it would lower the reporting threshold and add penalties including loss of Title IV funding.
ED opened a Section 117 investigation of Harvard University.

Executive Order 14282 was signed (published 2025-04-28), directing the Education Secretary to enforce Section 117 and hold noncompliant institutions accountable through audits, investigations and Attorney General enforcement.
ED announced that Section 117 enforcement was returning to its Office of General Counsel and opened an investigation of UC Berkeley, following a Harvard investigation announced the week before.
ED opened a Section 117 investigation of the University of Pennsylvania.

ED's new Section 117 reporting portal was scheduled to open on this date, per an ED announcement that warns noncompliant institutions of possible DOJ enforcement; CRS confirms the portal was established in January 2026.

ED and the State Department signed an interagency agreement under which State administers biannual reporting and the portal and can start civil investigations, with ED keeping leadership of enforcement.
ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice to renew the foreign gifts and contracts disclosure collection through the new portal.

A press report said the administration was probing Duke University and the University of North Dakota over China-related funding disclosures, quoting a State Department official that reviews found gaps.

title: Enforce HEA Section 117 foreign gift reporting, refer violators to DOJ, tie it to aid
uncertainties: The Harvard (2025-04-17) and Penn (2025-05-08) dates come from a law-firm summary in eCampus News; the ED Berkeley release has no publication date and says only that Harvard came a week earlier, so the Berkeley event is cited to the same summary and the ED page supports its content. The ED portal announcement page carries only a last-reviewed date of 2025-12-01 and announced the 2026-01-02 opening in advance. CRS reports four investigations without naming them. The Duke and North Dakota report does not say whether those reviews are formal Section 117 investigations or which agency leads them. No DOJ referral or civil action was found in the CRS paper or the sources read. Senate status of H.R. 1048 rests on the CRS paper (referred, no further action); congress.gov could not be fetched.
